{{Otheruses}}
{{MoreSources}}
[[File:Cumulonimbus.png|thumb|250px|Schematic of a cumulonimbus cloud]]
{{Quote|I saw&hellip;I saw a city in the clouds.|[[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]]|<ref name="Episode 5">{{Film|V}}</ref>}}
'''Clouds''' were visible masses of particles of condensed [[Water/Legends|watery]] vapor suspended in the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] of a [[Planet/Legends|planet]] or [[Moon/Legends|moon]]. [[Desert/Legends|Desert]] environments had very little cloud cover, which caused them to change [[Temperature/Legends|temperature]] rapidly, reaching temperatures of well over a hundred degrees by day, then losing up to eighty of those degrees during the night.<ref name="SWSA">''[[Star Wars Science Adventures: Journey Across Planet X]]''</ref>

When the droplets of water contained within a cloud became heavy enough to fall under [[Gravity/Legends|gravity]], causing a meteorological phenomenon called rain. Because they floated high above the general level of the ground, clouds were extremely cold inside. Because of that, some of the water vapor turned into ice crystals and ice pellets known as graupels, and fierce atmospheric winds would sometimes toss them around.<ref name="SWSA" />

Occasionally, two kinds of ice would collide, becoming charged with static electricity. Those crystals then became positively charged, while the graupels became negatively charged. Being lighter, the crystals were blown to the top of the cloud, which gave its upper part a positive charge, while the heavier graupels sank toward the bottom of the cloud, which became negatively charged. That configuration resulted in a huge discharge that manifested in the form of lightning. That phenomenon frequently occurred within a type of cloud called cumulonimbus.<ref name="SWSA" />

{{Noncanonstart|legends=1}}
On some planets, clouds could be also formed from particles of [[Mooxx fat]], a lighter-than-air substance. Warm climates on a [[Raspar system/Legends|Raspar system]] [[Unidentified planet (West Fissure)|world]] generated this phenomenon, which made the irrigation of [[arzen field]]s difficult.<ref name="MAGL">''[[Monsters and Aliens from George Lucas]]''</ref>
{{Noncanonend}}

==Behind the scenes==
In the [[2001]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]'', clouds appear as a unique terrain type that can be placed in player created levels. They also appeared in the sixth level of the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Imperial]] campaign, "Cloud City Attack," which depicts the [[Occupation of Bespin]].<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds]]''</ref>
